subject: Mismatch in ledger: overlapping provider maintenance vs transient partial degradation
messages:
From: Victor Ramos <victor.ramos@novaprod.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-19T16:02:00Z
Subject: Observed outage/latency spike 2026-09-19 — request for ledger review

Sergio / team,

We saw a sustained latency spike and partial failures impacting our /generate endpoint between 15:18 and 15:48 UTC on 2026-09-19. Our telemetry shows a ~40% increase in p95 and ~6% request errors during that 30-minute window. This is reflected in our internal SLA dashboard and is materially impacting our customer-facing retries.

EdgeCore informed us they had "maintenance" for a short time earlier in the day, but their published maintenance window doesn't align with the start of our degradation. Can you please: 1) confirm how Redwood is counting that window in the uptime ledger, and 2) share any internal logs/traces that show whether this was a Redwood service issue or caused by the EdgeCore chain?

I've attached a short trace dump and our observed time series (novaprod_observed_traces.zip). We would like to request a formal ledger re-evaluation and, if eligible, an SLA credit.

Thanks,
Victor Ramos
Head of Platform Reliability, NovaProd
victor.ramos@novaprod.com

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>
To: Victor Ramos <victor.ramos@novaprod.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-19T18:04:00Z
Subject: Re: Observed outage/latency spike 2026-09-19 — request for ledger review

Victor — thanks for the data and heads up. We're pulling our router and probe telemetry now. Initial triage: we have a maintenance tag from EdgeCore in our provider logs at 15:10–15:20 UTC, but your degradation begins at ~15:18 and continues past their maintenance window. That overlap (maintenance tail + transient partial degradation) is exactly the edge case that can cause ledger mismatches.

Action items from our side:
- I'll ask EdgeCore for their detailed maintenance start/stop and probe traces (cc'ed ops-support).
- Naomi, can you pull the per-probe availability and the per-pop request success rates for 14:50–16:00 UTC and mark sequences with KV-cache priming?
- Grace / Marissa, tagging for potential credit split and legal notice if the ledger needs manual correction.

I'll forward EdgeCore's reply into this thread and keep Victor updated. Short answer: we may need to treat this as a mixed event (partial degradation + provider maintenance) and split attribution rather than a clean maintenance exclusion.

— Sergio
Sergio Alvarez
Escalations Lead, Redwood Inference
sergio@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123

From: ops-support@edgecore.net <ops-support@edgecore.net>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>, Victor Ramos <victor.ramos@novaprod.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-20T07:19:00Z
Subject: Re: Observed outage/latency spike 2026-09-19 — request for ledger review

Hi team,

Thanks for flagging. Per our maintenance logs: we scheduled a config push affecting egress routing in POP-us-west-2 between 15:05 and 15:25 UTC. The job was marked complete at 15:23 UTC. We did see elevated retransmits on a small subset of peering links starting at ~15:18 UTC that cleared after 15:28 UTC. Attaching our maintenance CSV (edgecore-maint-report.csv) with the per-link timelines and a small probe sample export.

EdgeCore position: the job was within the published maintenance window (start 15:05, stop 15:25). Some customers saw degradations that extended slightly beyond completion while caches and routes reconverged — we can provide per-link timestamps but we consider this within maintenance scope unless Redwood's ledger logic attributes the tail to Redwood.

Link to our incident page: https://status.edgecore.net/incidents/EO-2026-09-19

--
EdgeCore Ops Support
ops-support@edgecore.net
attachments: edgecore-maint-report.csv

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-21T15:30:00Z
Subject: Re: Observed outage/latency spike 2026-09-19 — request for ledger review

Folks — consolidated findings after running the probe reconciliation and request logs:

Summary:
- NovaProd observed spike: 15:18–15:48 UTC (Victor payload).
- EdgeCore maintenance window: 15:05–15:25 UTC (edgecore report).
- Redwood per-pop traces show elevated p95 and error rate beginning 15:17 UTC; most affected POPs are us-west-2a / us-west-2b. Errors persist in a degraded tail until ~15:33 UTC.

Interpretation: this is a mixed event. The first ~8 minutes (15:17–15:25) overlap with EdgeCore maintenance and are plausibly attributable to their config change. The subsequent tail (15:25–15:33) is outside their declared window and appears to correlate with Redwood routing reconvergence + KV-cache warming on our edge layer.

Proposed ledger action: split the 16-minute disputed window as follows:
- EdgeCore attribution: 15:17–15:25 (8 minutes)
- Redwood attribution: 15:25–15:33 (8 minutes)
- Remaining NovaProd-observed degradation after 15:33 up to 15:48 appears to be upstream client retries and eventually resolved — not eligible for further credit.

Recommendation: offer NovaProd a partial SLA credit proportional to the Redwood-attributed minutes (50% of the disputed window). I've attached a quick proposal (proposed-credit-split.xlsx) and a short alignment digest with the probe times (alignment-digest.txt).

Next steps: Grace — can you approve the ledger correction and credit percentage so I can send the formal letter to Victor? Marissa — please prepare the accounting entry and draft the customer note. Victor, if that split looks acceptable to NovaProd we can proceed with the formal credit and ledger update.

Thanks,
Naomi Feldman
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference
naomi@redwood.com
